title: Latent space and the VAE
hook: Train a tiny VAE on a CPU, and see why the midpoint of two latents is a picture while the midpoint of two images is a ghost.

verified.claim: The scale factors are read from the format classes.
process_in multiplies by scale_factor, and SD3's and Flux's subtract a shift first.
DiagonalGaussianRegularizer returns the mode unless sample is set.
The KL formula matched a Monte Carlo estimate, and the small VAE's trade-off was measured.
nm_latent_ops ran on a CPU; b_latent_gain passes validate_prompt.

unchecked: The toy VAE has one true degree of freedom, so its behaviour does not transfer directly to image VAEs, as the lesson says.
We did not run wrong-VAE or out-of-memory cases for this lesson. Those lines describe the shapes and what we expect.
The statements about Rombach et al. were checked at the first audit and not re-read this time.
